Synopsis:
Colombia's central bank governor signals inflation won't reach the 3% target until mid-2028, revised upward from prior projections. Domestic demand significantly outpacing production is driving persistent price pressures. Compounding the challenge, Colombia's Vice-Minister of Finance acknowledged the fiscal rule — suspended in June 2025 for three years — is unlikely to be reinstated in the near term, raising medium-term fiscal credibility concerns. Colombia has missed its inflation target continuously since 2021, with current annual inflation at 6.03%.
